title: Battery Replacement Warranties: Core Deposit Collection, Refund and Forfeiture
content:
## 1. Collection

1.1 A core deposit of the line's core deposit amount is collected on every Crestline battery sold without an old battery handed in, on the ticket of that sale. The core deposit is the only money a Battery Replacement Warranty's deposit account holds: it is refundable when the core is returned in time and forfeited when it is not.

## 2. Return window

2.1 The core must be returned no later than the end of the core return window counted from the battery purchase on the original ticket.

2.2 The window is the line's core return window in calendar days. Calendar days are counted from the day after the anchor date, so the anchor date plus the number of days is the last qualifying date. The anchor date is the purchase date recorded on the battery's warranty, the date of the original ticket; it is read from Crestline's record of that warranty, not from the customer's account of when the battery was bought.

2.3 A return on the last qualifying date is in time. The deposit refunded is the one held on the warranty of the battery sold on that ticket.

2.4 Any lead-acid automotive battery is accepted as the core.

## 3. Refund and forfeiture

3.1 A core returned in time refunds the full deposit to the original tender. A refund to the Crestline Credit Card posts to the card account as a merchandise credit.

3.2 On the day after the window ends the deposit is forfeited in full.

3.3 Each deposit is settled once, by a refund or a forfeit, citing the core charge it settles. A deposit already settled by a refund or a forfeit is not settled again.

## 4. Boundary illustration

*Hypothetical inputs, for illustration only: a purchase dated 5 June and a window of 20 calendar days (not any line's window).* Day one of the window is 6 June, and the last qualifying date is 5 June plus 20 days, 25 June.

| Core returned on | Within the window? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 24 June | Yes | full deposit refunded to the original tender |
| 25 June (the last qualifying date) | Yes | full deposit refunded to the original tender |
| 26 June | No | 26 June is the day after the window ends; the deposit is forfeited in full on that day |

## 5. Points of judgement

- *Does the date the customer gives for the purchase decide the window?* No. The window runs from the purchase date on Crestline's record of the battery's warranty.
- *Is part of the deposit ever refunded?* No. A return in time refunds the full deposit, and the deposit is otherwise forfeited in full.
- *Must the returned core be the battery taken out of the vehicle?* No; any lead-acid automotive battery is accepted.
